summary.title: Health Check Response Format for HTTP APIs
summary.one_liner: You learn the draft IETF standard JSON format (application/health+json) for reporting HTTP API health, with status values, optional fields, and a nested checks object for downstream dependencies.
keywords: api health status pass fail warn
spring boot health status up down
health check alternative to http status codes
how to design api health endpoint
takeaways: Health responses use the media type application/health+json with a required root field "status" set to pass, fail, or warn.
HTTP status codes must match the status: 2xx-3xx for pass and warn, 4xx-5xx for fail.
A checks object reports each downstream dependency as an array of component details, with optional observedValue, observedUnit, and time fields.
Health endpoints should be cacheable (e.g., Cache-Control max-age) and secured, since health data can help attackers.
summary.summary: This is an IETF Internet-Draft (draft-inadarei-api-health-check-06, October 2021, Informational status) proposing a standard JSON response format for HTTP API health endpoints. It defines required and optional top-level fields such as status, releaseId, output, checks, links, serviceId and description, and explains how status values relate to HTTP response codes. It also describes the checks object for downstream dependencies, with a worked example output, security considerations, IANA media type registration, and guidance on serving and caching health responses.
